newsitem.title: INDIA: India edible oil trade body urges oilseed imports.
newsitem.headline: India edible oil trade body urges oilseed imports.

text.p: India should allow imports of oilseeds to meet the domestic shortfall of edible oil, a leading industry body on edible oil said on Monday.

The Central Organisation of Oil Industry and Trade (COOIT), in its proposals to the government ahead of the 1997/98 annual budget, said oilseeds import would also help in efficient use of idle oilseeds processing capacity.
The budget is expected to be presented by the Finance Minister P. Chidambaran on February 28.
COOIT has estimated the current idle capacity of the oilseeds processing units at 60 percent.

"It has been again urged that it would be advantageous from all angles to allow import of oilseeds as it would generate additional employment opportunities and augument edible oil availability...," COOIT said in a statement.
India annually consumes over 7.0 million tonnes of edible oil against a domestic output of around 6.2 million. The rest is met through imports. India does not permit oilseed imports.
